transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

What brought me in is… people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor will be talking right to me, or my wife, and then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said. Then I’m asking them to repeat it, and it’s causing problems.
When this happens, do you feel like you didn’t hear the words clearly?
No, it’s not like I can’t hear the words. They’re talking right to me. I just… I’ll realize a minute later I only took in half of it, and then I have to ask them to say it again.
Do you remember having this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah, I do. I was like this even when I was little. Teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t stay put, and I’d call out answers before I was supposed to. I remember getting in trouble for butting into other kids’ work too, like before middle school even.
Do you still find it hard to stay seated when you’re expected to, like in meetings or other situations where you’re supposed to remain sitting?

Yeah, I do. At work especially, when I’m supposed to stay at my station, I’ll step away to check something, grab a tool, or go talk to somebody, even though I know the line needs me right there. It’s like I know I should stay put, but I’m already moving before I really think it through.
Besides work, do these attention problems cause trouble for you at home?

Yeah, it does. At home my wife and kids get pretty frustrated with me because I’ll throw off the routine instead of helping things go smoothly. Like I’m supposed to be helping get things done, but I end up interrupting or making it harder.

And at work it’s gotten serious too. I’ve had formal warnings, and I worry I could lose my job or even cause a safety problem on the line.
When you miss parts of what people are saying, is it usually because you’re preoccupied with worry?

Not usually worry, no. It’s more like they’re talking right to me, my supervisor or my wife, and then a minute later I realize I only caught part of it. Then I have to ask them to repeat themselves, and that’s what brought me in, honestly—people keep saying I’m not listening.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a longstanding pattern since childhood of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity across settings, with current occupational and family impairment. Childhood onset is supported by teacher reports of not staying seated, calling out answers, and intruding before middle school. This presentation is more consistent with ADHD than an isolated attention/concentration symptom code.
